A1-1-0.name: Chain of three
A1-1-0.prompt: Di tres oraciones sobre una persona: nombre, relación y un detalle. Cambia de persona y repite.
items: This is Sofía. She is my sister. Her hair is very long.
That is Camilo. He is my classmate. His English is good.
Now use: my mother — her job.
Now use: my friends — their city.
Now use: my dog — its name.
answers: This is Sofía. She is my sister. Her hair is very long.
That is Camilo. He is my classmate. His English is good.
This is my mother. She is a nurse. Her job is very interesting.
These are my friends. They are from Cali. Their city is very hot.
This is my dog. It is very small. Its name is Toby.

A1-1-1.name: Three questions, three answers
A1-1-1.prompt: Pregúntale a tu compañero y escribe solo la respuesta corta.
answers: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.
Yes, it is. / No, it isn’t.
It’s near my house.
They are ten and fifteen.
It’s Ms. Gómez.

A1-2-0.name: Add the -s
A1-2-0.prompt: Cambia la oración de «I» a «my brother» y dila en voz alta.
items: I go to the gym on Tuesdays. →
I study English twice a week. →
answers: My brother works at home.
My brother watches TV after dinner.
My brother goes to the gym on Tuesdays.
My brother studies English twice a week.
My brother finishes at six.

A1-2-1.name: at, on or in?
A1-2-1.prompt: Di la expresión con la preposición correcta: at, on o in.
answers: at seven o’clock
on Saturday
in July
in the afternoon
at night

A1-3-0.name: Near or far, one or many
A1-3-0.prompt: Señala y di la oración completa con la palabra correcta.
items: ___ is my chair (the one you touch)
answers: This pen is mine.
Those pens are blue.
That book is new.
These books are heavy.
This is my chair.

A1-3-1.name: Make it comparative
A1-3-1.prompt: Compara las dos cosas en voz alta en una sola oración.
answers: A taxi is more expensive than a bus.
Medellín is warmer than Bogotá.
This phone is better than my old phone.
The market is cheaper than the mall.
Today is worse than yesterday.

A1-4-0.name: Replace the name
A1-4-0.prompt: Repite la oración con un pronombre en lugar de las palabras subrayadas.
items: He works with you and me. →
They call my sister and me. →
answers: I see her every day.
She helps him.
We invite them.
He works with us.
They call us.

A1-4-1.name: Offer and answer
A1-4-1.prompt: Haz la oferta y luego da una respuesta educada.
answers: Would you like a glass of water? — Yes, please.
Would you like to sit down? — No, thank you. I’m fine.
Would you like some help? — Yes, please. That’s very kind.
Would you like to see the menu? — Yes, please.
Would you like anything else? — No, thank you.

A1-5-0.name: Now or every day?
A1-5-0.prompt: Di cada oración dos veces: una como rutina y otra como «ahora mismo».
items: I work at home. → I’m working at home right now.
answers: I’m working at home right now.
She’s studying English right now.
They’re watching a film right now.
He’s cooking dinner right now.
We’re looking after my cousin right now.

A1-5-1.name: Up and down the scale
A1-5-1.prompt: Responde «¿Cuántas personas de tu familia hacen esto?» usando un cuantificador distinto cada vez.
answers: Not many people in my family speak English.
Nearly all my relatives live in this city.
No one in my family works at night.
A lot of my cousins use TikTok.
Few people in my family play a sport.

A1-6-0.name: Slide the adverb
A1-6-0.prompt: Pon el adverbio en el lugar correcto y di la oración.
items: They / go to the cinema (hardly ever)
We / are at home on Sundays (usually)
answers: I usually study at night.
She is always late.
They hardly ever go to the cinema.
He never eats meat.
We are usually at home on Sundays.

A1-6-1.name: Ask with how
A1-6-1.prompt: Haz la pregunta con how y da una respuesta corta.
answers: How often do you go to the gym? — Three times a week.
How long are your English classes? — About two hours.
How well do you cook? — Not very well.
How often does your family call you? — Every Sunday.
How long is your journey to school? — About twenty minutes.

A1-7-0.name: Three ways
A1-7-0.prompt: Di cada oración en afirmativo, negativo y como pregunta.
items: I / go to the gym yesterday
answers: I went to the gym yesterday. / I didn’t go to the gym yesterday. / Did I go to the gym yesterday?
She called me last night. / She didn’t call me last night. / Did she call me last night?
They finished the project. / They didn’t finish the project. / Did they finish the project?
We saw your message. / We didn’t see your message. / Did we see your message?
He ate at home. / He didn’t eat at home. / Did he eat at home?

A1-7-1.name: was or were
A1-7-1.prompt: Completa en voz alta y luego conviértela en pregunta.
answers: I was at work. → Was I at work?
They were very friendly. → Were they very friendly?
It was cold last night. → Was it cold last night?
You were right. → Were you right?
We were in the same class. → Were we in the same class?

A1-8-0.name: Map it
A1-8-0.prompt: Mira el salón (o un mapa) y di una oración con cada preposición.
answers: There is a lamp next to the sofa.
There is a car in front of my house.
There are some trees behind the building.
There is a bank across from the park.
There is a pharmacy between the bakery and the bank.

A1-8-1.name: Countable or not?
A1-8-1.prompt: Haz la pregunta con how much o how many.
answers: How many people live here?
How much traffic is there?
How many restaurants are there?
How much noise is there at night?
How many parks are there near you?

A1-9-0.name: Two questions, one person
A1-9-0.prompt: Para cada persona, haz las dos preguntas y da una respuesta en dos partes: primero el físico, luego la personalidad.
answers: What does your English teacher look like? — She is tall with short brown hair. What is she like? — She is patient and funny.
What does your best friend look like? — He is short with curly black hair. What is he like? — He is friendly and very talkative.
What does your favourite actor look like? — He is tall with dark eyes. What is he like? — He is funny and kind.
What does the person on your left look like? — She has long straight hair and glasses. What is she like? — She is quiet and very smart.
What does your mother look like? — She is short with long black hair. What is she like? — She is calm and very generous.

A1-9-1.name: Point without pointing
A1-9-1.prompt: Identifica a un compañero usando solo «the one…». El grupo adivina. Sin nombres y sin señalar.
answers: The one wearing the red jacket.
The one sitting next to the window.
The one talking to the teacher.
The one with long curly hair.
The ones standing near the door.

A1-10-0.name: The checklist
A1-10-0.prompt: Mira la lista de tareas (cinco cosas, tres con chulo). Di cada una con «already» o «yet».
answers: I’ve already bought the tickets.
I’ve already packed the bags.
I haven’t called the hotel yet.
I’ve already printed the map.
I haven’t changed money yet.

A1-10-1.name: Perfect then past
A1-10-1.prompt: Pregunta con el presente perfecto; responde con el pasado simple y un detalle.
answers: Have you ever visited Medellín? — Yes, I visited it last year. I loved the metro.
Have you ever tried sushi? — Yes, I tried it in Bogotá two years ago.
Have you ever lost your phone? — Yes, I lost it on a bus last month.
Have you ever met someone famous? — Yes, I met a famous singer at the airport in 2022.
Have you ever travelled by plane at night? — Yes, I travelled to Madrid at night last December.

A1-11-0.name: Turn up the dial
A1-11-0.prompt: Di la misma oración cinco veces cambiando solo el adverbio: a bit → quite → very → really → extremely.
answers: The exam was a bit / quite / very / really / extremely difficult.
The bus is a bit / quite / very / really / extremely slow.
This coffee is a bit / quite / very / really / extremely strong.
My flat is a bit / quite / very / really / extremely small.
The film was a bit / quite / very / really / extremely long.

A1-11-1.name: Option then advice
A1-11-1.prompt: Para cada situación, da una opción con «can» y una recomendación con «should».
items: a visitor has one free day in your city
a classmate wants to improve listening
a tourist has lost their phone
someone wants cheap lunch near school
answers: You can take the cable car. You should visit the botanical garden.
You can take a pill. You should drink some water and rest.
You can watch series in English. You should listen to podcasts every day.
You can use my phone to call it. You should go to the police station.
You can buy an empanada at the tienda. You should try the restaurant next to the school.

A1-12-0.name: Same advice, three frames
A1-12-0.prompt: Da la misma recomendación de tres formas: «It’s a good idea to…», «The best way is to…», «You need to…».
answers: It’s a good idea to book in advance. / The best way is to book in advance. / You need to book in advance.
It’s a good idea to arrive twenty minutes early. / The best way is to arrive twenty minutes early. / You need to arrive twenty minutes early.
It’s a good idea to bring cash. / The best way is to bring cash. / You need to bring cash.
It’s a good idea to speak to the teacher first. / The best way is to speak to the teacher first. / You need to speak to the teacher first.
It’s a good idea to take the earlier train. / The best way is to take the earlier train. / You need to take the earlier train.

A1-12-1.name: Politeness ladder
A1-12-1.prompt: Haz la misma petición tres veces, de directa a muy educada: Can you… → Could you… → Would you mind…
answers: Can you open the window? / Could you open the window, please? / Would you mind opening the window?
Can you repeat the question? / Could you repeat the question, please? / Would you mind repeating the question?
Can you lend me a pen? / Could you lend me a pen, please? / Would you mind lending me a pen?
Can you wait five minutes? / Could you wait five minutes, please? / Would you mind waiting five minutes?
Can you send me the file? / Could you send me the file, please? / Would you mind sending me the file?

A1-13-0.name: Match the helper
A1-13-0.prompt: Muestra que estás de acuerdo dos veces: una con so / neither y otra con «Me too / Me neither».
answers: So am I. / Me too.
Neither do I. / Me neither.
So have I. / Me too.
Neither can I. / Me neither.
So did I. / Me too.

A1-13-1.name: Order and ask
A1-13-1.prompt: En un café: pide con «I’d like», luego haz una petición con «Would you mind…?» y otra con «Could you…?».
answers: I’d like a table by the window, please.
Would you mind bringing the menu in English?
Could you bring the bill, please?
I’d like a glass of water, please.
Could you tell me the wifi password, please?

A1-14-0.name: Two then one
A1-14-0.prompt: Compara las dos primeras cosas y luego di cuál es la número uno de las tres.
items: the bus / the metro / a taxi — fast
your town / this city / the capital — noisy
answers: Bogotá is colder than Medellín, and it’s the coldest of the three.
The metro is faster than the bus, and it’s the fastest of the three.
Coffee is more expensive than tea, but juice is the most expensive of the three.
Monday is busier than Friday, and it’s the busiest of the three.
This city is noisier than my town, but the capital is the noisiest of the three.

A1-14-1.name: Ask the measurement
A1-14-1.prompt: Pregunta por cada cosa con el «how» correcto y responde con un número y el adjetivo repetido.
items: the tallest building in your city
answers: How long is the Magdalena river? — It’s about 1,500 kilometres long.
How tall is the tallest building in your city? — It’s about 200 metres tall.
How long is your classroom? — It’s about ten metres long.
How far is the coast? — It’s about 1,000 kilometres away.
How hot is it today? — It’s about 25 degrees.

A1-15-0.name: Intention or arrangement
A1-15-0.prompt: Di cada plan dos veces: como intención con «going to» y como cita acordada con el presente continuo.
answers: I’m going to see the doctor. / I’m seeing the doctor on Monday at nine.
I’m going to travel to the coast. / I’m travelling to the coast on Friday.
I’m going to start a course. / I’m starting a course next Monday.
I’m going to meet a friend. / I’m meeting a friend at the mall at six.
I’m going to move house. / I’m moving house on Saturday.

A1-15-1.name: Pass it on
A1-15-1.prompt: Escucha un mensaje y pásalo con «tell» y otra vez con «say».
items: The meeting has moved to Friday.
answers: He told me that the class starts at eight. / He said that the class starts at eight.
She told us to bring our ID. / She said that we need to bring our ID.
He told me that he can’t come today. / He said that he can’t come today.
She told me that the meeting has moved to Friday. / She said that the meeting has moved to Friday.
He told me to call him after six. / He said that I should call him after six.

A1-16-0.name: Then, now, since
A1-16-0.prompt: Di tres oraciones sobre un tema: cómo era (pasado simple o used to), cómo es (presente simple) y qué ha cambiado (presente perfecto).
answers: My neighbourhood used to be very quiet. Now it is very busy. They have built a new shopping centre.
I used to play football every day. Now I watch series in my free time. I have started going to the gym.
I didn’t speak English at school. Now I understand a lot. My English has improved this year.
There was no metro in my city in 1990. Now I take the metro every day. Transport has become faster.
I studied at a public school. Now I work at a bank. I have worked there for three years.

A1-16-1.name: Certainty ladder
A1-16-1.prompt: Di la misma idea de futuro en tres niveles: firme («I’m going to…»), probable («I plan to…») y lejano («I hope to…»).
answers: I’m going to change jobs. / I plan to change jobs. / I hope to change jobs.
I’m going to travel abroad. / I plan to travel abroad. / I hope to travel abroad.
I’m going to learn another language. / I plan to learn another language. / I hope to learn another language.
I’m going to move house. / I plan to move house. / I hope to move house.
I’m going to finish this course. / I plan to finish this course. / I hope to finish this course.
